Both are Hardin's empirical counts. Computed independently by transfer matrices: A217450(n+3) = A200865(n) through n = 79, and the same identity holds for 4- and 5-letter alphabets. It follows from factoring the 3-window erosion into two 2-window erosions plus Galois-connection (opening/closing) arguments, linking a mathematical-morphology image count to a pattern-avoidance count; the proof is short.

A112046 values are primes. Value p first appears at m = p^2, i.e. index (p^2-1)/2, unless some prime r in (p^2-p, p^2) has least quadratic non-residue exactly p; every other m < p^2 is ruled out by multiplicativity and the bound n(r)(n(r)-1) < r. So the identity A112051(n) = (prime(n)^2-1)/2 for n >= 4 (for p = 5 the exception r = 23 does occur) reduces to n(r) < sqrt(r)-1. That needs explicit Burgess-type bounds (e.g. Norton, Trevino) for r > ~1e8, plus my direct check of all p <= 14107 (A112046 computed to index 1e8). A short proof exists, but it uses analytic number theory; the connection is Jacobi symbols to Pythagorean legs, neither entry notes it.

Proved, for every alphabet 0..k. Let δ be the 2-window max with 0-padding (length L -> L+1) and ε the 2-window min (its adjoint). δ maps words with no strict interior valley bijectively onto words where every nonzero entry is <= some neighbour (A202882's condition), with inverse ε. Complementing (x -> k-x) turns valley-free words into peak-free words, giving A200880(n)=A202882(n+3). This links peak-avoiding words to the images of morphological dilation. Bijection checked by brute force; the identity holds for k=1..7 up to n=40, and for k=2 up to n=100.

Proved. A218051(m) counts the images of the 3-window min-filter, Im ε3, on 0..3 words of length m. The map z -> (max(z_j,z_{j+1}))_j sends Im ε3 bijectively onto the length m-1 words with no strict interior peak or valley. The inverse is w -> 2-window min of w padded with the top value 3. Map a binary word w of length n+1 to d_i = w_{i+1} - w_i + 1. For n>=2 this is a bijection from overlap-free binary words to squarefree ternary words avoiding 010 and 212. Hilltop maps on a path with values 0..2: a zero-run between two hilltops must look like 1,0,0,1 at most, so it has length <=4; a run at an end has length <=2; and the indicator cannot be all zeros. Conversely every such word is realized by setting all hilltops to 2. So for n>=3 the count equals A102026, which proves Hardin's 'empirical' 5-bonacci recurrence for A218199. Brute force confirms this for n<=13.

If k <= 2^n+1, any prime p with p^n | k^3-1 has p^n < (2^n+1)^3. For p=2 (and p = 2 mod 3) cubing is injective, so k = 1 mod p^n. For p=3 the least k is 3^{n-1}+1. For p = 1 mod 3, a nontrivial root needs p^n | k^2+k+1, giving k > 2^n. So A088039(n) = 2^n+1 for n>=3, which proves Barker's conjecture in A088039. Verified to n=300.
Exactly two of k, k+1, k+2 are prime iff (k, k+2) are twin primes with k>=3 (since k+1 is even), or k=1 or k=2. So A152916 = {1,4} together with A126249.

General identity, for every value range 0..k: the map y -> (min(y_i,y_{i+1})) is a bijection from length-(L+1) sequences with no strict peak after padding with 0 at both ends (A203050) onto length-L sequences with no strict valley.
